newsitem.title: USA: Clinton vows aid for flood victims.
newsitem.headline: Clinton vows aid for flood victims.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Tuesday departed for North Dakota to inspect flood damage, vowing to "do everything we can" to help the victims of the natural disaster.
Speaking at the White House, Clinton said he was going to the ravaged area "to view the flood damage, to pledge our nation's support, (and) see that we can do everything we can do to help them."
"People are quite literally in the fight of their lives," Clinton said before departing the White House. "What they have endured is enormous. How they are enduring it is remarkable."

"Americans have a habit of joining together at times like this," Clinton said, noting the entire nation has been "deeply moved by the pictures" of the devastation, particularly in Grand Forks -- a city that has been evacuated.
About 90 percent of Grank Forks, a city of 50,000, was under water from the bulging Red River, which extended its widening path of destruction northward into Canada.
In response to a question, Clinton said "we're going to have to be prepared to be very creative" in coming up with the best way to deal with such a massive problem.
